input.command: export PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH"; gbrain setup --help 2>&1 | head -60; which claude
input.description: Show gbrain setup options and check for claude CLI

content.content:
gbrain setup <harness> — give an agent harness memory in one command

Usage: gbrain setup claude-code [flags]
       gbrain setup codex [flags]

Resolves the brain, source, transport, launcher and registration owner first and
prints them; refuses before writing anything when another owner holds the target.
With no brain configured it creates a keyless local one (gbrain init --pglite
--no-embedding). It then writes the MCP entry and hooks into the harness's own
config and verifies them with the harness_wiring smoke. Codex: [mcp_servers.<name>]
and the hook trust entries in $CODEX_HOME/config.toml, the hooks in hooks.json.

Flags:
  --dry-run            Print the target and every step; write nothing.
  --json               One JSON document on stdout (target, decisions, steps, states).
  --surface S          MCP tool surface: verbs, starter or full, listed in full (default:
                       GBRAIN_SURFACE, then the surface already registered, then starter
                       with only the memory verbs and request_tools listed:
                       serve --surface starter --advertise verbs; full is the opt-in for
                       every operation).
  --scope user|project Wiring scope: every Claude Code session (user, default) or only
                       sessions in this directory (project: ~/.claude.json projects
                       entry + .claude/settings.local.json). Codex: user only.
  --no-hooks           Register MCP only; install no hooks (GBRAIN_HOOKS=0 does the same).
  --capture            Accept automatic capture: also install the capture hooks
                       (Claude Code: Stop and SessionEnd; Codex: SessionEnd).
  --no-capture         Decline automatic capture (the default).
  --providers          Accept provider use: a new brain is created with embeddings.
  --no-providers       Decline provider use (the default: keyless, no paid calls).
  --name NAME          MCP server name (default gbrain); one name per install.
  --source ID          Pin the source the MCP server and hooks use.
  --gbrain-bin PATH    Absolute gbrain launcher (default: the gbrain on PATH).
  --serves one|several Whom the brain serves (default one: nothing changes). several labels each
                       person: config access.serves = several, a member, a folder rule
                       people/<member>/ only that member reads and one key bound to that member
                       (a 0600 file under <config>/member-keys/), then one bound read per member
                       proves it. A one-person setup on a brain that already serves several
                       people (2+ enabled members) refuses rather than write a connection bound
                       to nobody, unless this harness's entry or config mcp.stdio_member binds it.
  --members IDS        The people of --serves several, comma-separated (e.g. alice-example,bob-example).
  --labelled-only      With --serves several: each member's key reads only pages labelled for
                       that member (readable_by or a rule), never the owner's. Opt-in.
  --members-file PATH  The same, one id per line.
  --stdio-member ID    claude-code or codex: write serve --stdio-member ID into this harness's
                       MCP entry, so only its sessions read as ID (an enabled member, or one
                       of --members). Other harnesses on this host are unchanged. Use it for a
                       harness only ID uses; refused where OpenClaw or Hermes is installed
                       (give each person their own HTTP key there). A re-run keeps the entry's
                       member; setup never adds one on its own.
  --no-stdio-member    Remove --stdio-member from this harness's entry.
  --remove             Remove exactly what setup wrote (unchanged entries only), the
                       brain-first instruction block included. The brain and your
                       notes stay. Combine with --dry-run to preview.
  --no-instructions    Opt out of the brain-first instruction block (see below); an
                       existing block is removed and the opt-out is remembered.
                       GBRAIN_AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS=0 does the same.
  --instructions       Opt back in after an earlier --no-instructions.
  --instructions-only  Manage only the brain-first block (on OpenClaw and Hermes, with
                       its per-turn hook): no brain, MCP or other hook changes.
                       Works for a hosted connection too, and for any harness below.
/opt/harness/bin/claude

content.content:
[gbrain notice release_channel] This install now follows the stable channel: weekly releases promoted after testing. To get every release instead, run: gbrain config set self_upgrade.channel alpha
Target (Claude Code, user scope):
  brain      new keyless PGLite brain at /harness-state/.gbrain/brain.pglite (gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding)
  source     the brain's default source (unpinned)
  transport  stdio MCP: /harness-state/.gbrain/hook-launcher/gbrain-hook /harness-state/.bun/bin/gbrain serve --surface starter --advertise verbs (lists the memory verbs and request_tools; every starter tool stays callable)
  owner      none yet; setup will own 'gbrain'
  files      /harness-state/claude/.claude.json (MCP), /harness-state/claude/settings.json (hooks)
Decisions:
  wiring     user scope; hooks SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit [default]
  capture    declined (no Stop/SessionEnd hooks, no transcript capture; accept with --capture) [default]
  providers  declined (keyless: setup configures no paid provider; accept with --providers) [default]
  would write instructions brain-first block in new file /harness-state/claude/CLAUDE.md [default; opt out with --no-instructions]
[AGENT]
why: [first_run_decisions] Setup is complete and memory works now. One optional choice remains; nothing is written until the user answers.
1. Give this brain a shape? A personal brain gets three empty starter pages (facts about you, your voice, how you decide) and a notes folder you pick, imported read only. A company brain gets empty pages for company facts, decisions, pricing, customers, calls and playbooks in a company source, and a docs folder you pick. Setup tells the agent to read them. Nothing is invented. (id: brain_shape)
   - personal: Personal brain, no notes folder yet (run: gbrain setup claude-code --shape personal)
   - company: Company brain, just me (add --docs <folder> for company docs, --transcripts <folder> for call transcripts) (run: gbrain setup claude-code --shape company)
   - both: Personal and company brain, just me (run: gbrain setup claude-code --shape both)
   - company_team: Company brain shared with a team (prints where it lives; creates nothing) (run: gbrain setup claude-code --shape company --team)
   - none: No starter pages (memory works as it is)
   default: none — Nothing is written until the user picks; memory already works without it.
[SHOW USER]
gbrain is set up, so memory works now. Want a personal or company brain? I can add starter pages (facts, voice and decisions) and import a notes or docs folder you pick.
[/SHOW USER]
[/AGENT]

summary: Run gbrain setup for Claude Code with keyless defaults

content.content:
Next: open a new Claude Code session (config is read at session start) and check that /mcp lists gbrain.
Memory: save what the user asks you to remember as a fact with gbrain remember "<fact>", naming its entity and provenance (MCP tool: remember). World-visible facts (the default) are pushed into new sessions; a private fact is not (local CLI recall only). capture writes a page, not a fact.
Opt-ins (nothing is on until you turn it on): keys and embeddings, autopilot, dream schedule, connectors, auto-upgrade, release channel: https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/v0.60.734.0/INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md#opt-ins
[AGENT]
why: [first_run_decisions] Setup is complete: the brain is ready and Claude Code is wired, so memory works now. These first-run settings are in effect as listed; none blocks memory or needs a new session to answer. Relay them once, in the reply that reports this install, as the current settings and how to change them; do not hold the install open or end it waiting on an answer. When the user picks an option, run its command. Automatic saving (`writeback`) is separate from setup's capture decision (Stop/SessionEnd hooks); while unanswered it comes back in a later session until the user answers or mutes it.
1. Which search mode should this brain use? Estimated downstream input cost of the retrieved payload at 10K queries/month (Haiku 5.5 / Sonnet 5.5 / Opus 5.5): conservative $4 / $80 / $160, balanced $10 / $200 / $400, tokenmax $20 / $400 / $800 per month. (id: search_mode)
   - conservative: conservative (applied) (run: gbrain config set search.mode conservative)
   - balanced: balanced (run: gbrain config set search.mode balanced)
   - tokenmax: tokenmax (run: gbrain config set search.mode tokenmax)
   default: conservative — No chat key (Anthropic/OpenAI/Google) and no ready reranker — conservative keeps a tight 4K budget; balanced's reranker could not run.
2. Should agents save important facts the user states (preferences, decisions, commitments) automatically, with provenance? Saved facts are readable by agents connected to this brain; transient facts expire. Off any time with `gbrain config set memory.auto_writeback off`. (id: writeback)
   - salient: Save durable facts the user states directly (recommended) (run: gbrain config set memory.auto_writeback salient)
   - all: Every direct factual statement (more low-value facts, more extraction spend) (run: gbrain config set memory.auto_writeback all)
   - off: Save only what the user explicitly asks to remember (records the answer) (run: gbrain config set memory.auto_writeback off)
   default: off — In effect now: agents save only what the user asks them to remember. salient is recommended for a personal brain; it is opt-in, so it turns on only when the user picks it.
3. Upkeep: free upkeep runs on its own while your agent's gbrain session is open. Nothing is deleted or paid for without you. Turn off: gbrain config set maintenance.auto false. Optional schedule: gbrain maintain --schedule. (id: upkeep)
   - on: Keep free upkeep on (in effect now)
   - off: Turn free upkeep off (run: gbrain config set maintenance.auto false)
   default: on — In effect now: the agent's gbrain serve runs the free upkeep tier while idle; nothing needs an answer.
4. Conversation archive: on. gbrain keeps one redacted page per conversation per day from your agent sessions (Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw, Hermes, Grok) in the conversations source, written by the maintenance pass. Without an embedding key nothing leaves this machine. Turn off: gbrain transcripts archive off. (id: conversation_archive)
   - on: Keep the conversation archive on (in effect now)
   - off: Turn the conversation archive off (run: gbrain transcripts archive off)
   default: on — In effect now: on by default on a personal brain; nothing needs an answer.
5. Give this brain a shape? A personal brain gets three empty starter pages (facts about you, your voice, how you decide) and a notes folder you pick, imported read only. A company brain gets empty pages for company facts, decisions, pricing, customers, calls and playbooks in a company source, and a docs folder you pick. Setup tells the agent to read them. Nothing is invented. (id: brain_shape)
   - personal: Personal brain, no notes folder yet (run: gbrain setup claude-code --shape personal)
   - company: Company brain, just me (add --docs <folder> for company docs, --transcripts <folder> for call transcripts) (run: gbrain setup claude-code --shape company)
   - both: Personal and company brain, just me (run: gbrain setup claude-code --shape both)
   - company_team: Company brain shared with a team (prints where it lives; creates nothing) (run: gbrain setup claude-code --shape company --team)
   - none: No starter pages (memory works as it is)
   default: none — Nothing is written until the user picks; memory already works without it.
[SHOW USER]
gbrain is set up and Claude Code is wired, so memory works now. In effect: search mode conservative; agents save only what you ask them to remember, until you turn on automatic saving (salient is recommended: durable facts you state, saved with provenance). Report back (Wakeshift): off. gbrain wakeshift enable turns it on. Upkeep: free upkeep runs on its own while your agent's gbrain session is open. Nothing is deleted or paid for without you. Turn off: gbrain config set maintenance.auto false. Optional schedule: gbrain maintain --schedule. Conversation archive: on. gbrain keeps one redacted page per conversation per day from your agent sessions (Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw, Hermes, Grok) in the conversations source, written by the maintenance pass. Without an embedding key nothing leaves this machine. Turn off: gbrain transcripts archive off. Estimated downstream input cost of the retrieved payload at 10K queries/month (Haiku 5.5 / Sonnet 5.5 / Opus 5.5): conservative $4 / $80 / $16…
[/SHOW USER]
[/AGENT]
[AGENT]
why: [hosted_option] gbrain.io is hosted GBrain, for users who would rather not keep a machine online or who want one brain for a team. Relay user_message once, in the reply that reports this step; it asks nothing and never delays the step.
[SHOW USER]
Hosted option: gbrain.io runs GBrain for you, with nothing to keep online, and can import this brain: https://gbrain.io/?ref=cli-setup. Mute: gbrain notices mute hosted_option.
[/SHOW USER]
[/AGENT]

gbrain is set up with free, keyless defaults and connected to Claude Code. I tested it: I saved a fact, and searching for it brought it back.

**What setup did** (`gbrain setup claude-code`):
- **Brain:** created a local brain at `~/.gbrain/brain.pglite`. It needs no API keys and makes no paid calls.
- **Claude Code:** registered gbrain for all your projects. `claude mcp get gbrain` reports it as **Connected**. Setup also added two hooks (at session start and when you send a prompt) and an instruction block in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` telling Claude to check the brain first.
- **Declined:** automatic transcript capture and paid providers.

**Settings in effect** (each can be changed with one command):
- **Search mode:** conservative, the only option that fully works without a key. `gbrain config set search.mode balanced` switches it.
- **Automatic saving:** off, so agents save only what you ask them to remember. gbrain recommends `gbrain config set memory.auto_writeback salient`, which saves lasting facts you state, noting where each came from.
- **Free upkeep:** on while a gbrain session is open; it never deletes anything or spends money. `gbrain config set maintenance.auto false` turns it off.
- **Conversation archive:** on. It keeps one redacted page per conversation per day, and with no keys nothing leaves this machine. `gbrain transcripts archive off` turns it off.
- **Brain shape:** none, so no starter pages. `gbrain setup claude-code --shape personal` adds them.

**Checks:**
- **Test fact:** I saved "gbrain v0.60.734.0 was installed on this machine" and found it again by searching. It's still in the brain because it's harmless and true.
- **Fix I applied without asking:** gbrain's health check (`gbrain doctor`) flagged that test fact's source label as needing repair. I previewed the repair, then applied it with nothing to re-embed. It changed only that one entry, and its trust level stayed the same.
- **Health score:** 90/100. Two warnings remain, and I don't think either needs action:
  - The quality score is 25/100 because the brain has no embeddings and is nearly empty. That's expected without keys and will rise as you add notes.
  - It says Claude Code has no gbrain registration, but also that it couldn't verify this from inside a running session. `claude mcp get` shows the registration and connection are fine.

**Next step for you:** start a new Claude Code session, since config is read at startup, and check that `/mcp` lists gbrain.
